newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight unchanged as liquidity improves.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight unchanged as liquidity improves.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate was unchanged at 8.5 percent as liquidity improved further in the interbank market due to injection of funds by the central bank, dealers said on Thursday.
They said the market was quiet as some central bank agents continued to dominate lending.
There was no confirmation from Bank Negara, which does not usually comment on its open market operations.
Earlier, other interbank rates were steady to slightly lower due the funds injection.
Dealers said in the morning that Bank Negara was said to have lent directly to discount houses. Its agent banks were also lending one-month money, they added.
One-month money was at 7.8/8.0 percent against 8.0, three-month was at 7.8/8.0 percent against 7.9/8.1 and six-month at 7.8/8.0 percent against 8.0 percent.
Bank Negara is said to have injected funds over the past week to help ease market tightness.
Recent heavy buying of the ringgit by the central bank to defend the currency from speculative attack had caused a liquidity squeeze.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were steady to slightly higher, reflecting the fall in interest rates, futures dealers said.
At the close, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was up two at 92.40, or an implied yield of 7.60 percent.
The December contract was up two at 92.62, or 7.58 percent.
